answer: A quorum is judged by graph shape, not headcount. Reviewers seal votes with an epoch cipher, so the protocol groups them into clusters, names hidden. A verdict stands only if its k reviewers sit in k separate clusters, none touching the author's. Fifty clones praising one another form one blob and get read as a single voice. Reputation behaves like a bag of marbles: a cluster contributes at most one, so synonymous accounts add nothing. Passing means recruiting strangers with unrelated history, each risking their standing. An orchard of fresh keys grows no independent branches overnight.
